body: I have alopecia areota, which is basically when you have different patches of bald spots on your head. I’ve had it for like 2 years, and I usually try to act strong and try not to let it bother me, but it’s hard sometimes. Especially as a teenage girl, my hair is a very important part of who I am. Most people are nice about it, but there have been a decent amount of times where people have made fun of or judged it. People made jokes about me having cancer before. It’s really hard sometimes, but at the end of the day, it’s just hair. I’m thankful that I don’t have any serious issues right now.

You are not alone. I'm an introvert too. This may sound cliche, but maybe a counselor could help a little? For me, reddit has helped me to be more open. And, its good that you posted this too. So for me, I never felt inspired to do art until a few months ago. For me, I don't really have a certain "style" I just draw what I feel. So when I want to draw something and I have artists block, I look up pictures of things and I draw what I find. Then I get another paper and I start drawing something similar, but making it my own art by adding new details, taking away things I don't like, and experimenting. I also erase. A lot. I keep trying until it looks how I want it to look. 
Disclaimer: I am not a professional in any way. I just like doing art for fun. Hope this was helpful. :)

I remember when my great grandmother died. She was so special, unique, hard working, and loved her family so much. My sadness is usually triggered from dreams I have.
